B: Hello hello! Can you hear me okay? I'm Chiamaka, in Leeds.
A: Yeah. Tracey. Sittingbourne, in Kent.
B: Kent! The garden of England, they call it, right? So what do you do, Tracey?
A: Shelf stacking. Early mornings at a supermarket. What about you, you're a nurse or something? I saw the top.
B: Doctor, actually! Acute medicine. But honestly, the nurses run the place, I just get the credit, ha. I've just come off four nights so I'm a bit loopy.
A: Four nights. I'm up at quarter past four and I moan about it.
B: No, quarter past four is a proper night shift, that counts! You're on your feet the whole time as well, lifting, everything.
A: Yeah. Quicker than most of them, to be honest. I just want it done so I can go home at eleven.
B: I love that. Get in, get it done, go home. I wish I could do that, but there's always one more discharge summary.
A: Can I ask you something, since you're a doctor?
B: Go on, everyone does! My whole family WhatsApp asks me.
A: My mum's getting forgetful. Like, leaving the gas on, asking the same thing three times. She's had the memory test at the GP and they've referred her, but it's been months. Is that normal, the wait?
B: Erm. Honestly? Yeah, the memory clinic waits are long, it's not just you. What I'd say is, if something happens, like a fall, or she gets suddenly confused, really suddenly, over a day or two, that's different, that can be an infection, and you get her seen quickly. Don't wait on the clinic for that. And keep a little list of what you notice, dates and that, because when you finally get in, they'll ask, and you'll forget. Everyone forgets in the room.
A: Right. That's useful. My sister's no help.
B: It's always one daughter doing it, isn't it. I'm the eldest, I know. Even from Leeds I'm the one sorting everything back home in Nigeria.
A: Do you get back much?
B: About every eighteen months. Not enough, really.
A: Long way, though.
B: It is. My poor mum. Anyway! Do you go on holiday? Please say yes, I need to live through someone.
A: Tenerife. Been four times. All-inclusive, sunbed, done.
B: Tenerife! I've not done Tenerife. I did Dubai last year, and Barcelona, with my girls. Lots of dressing up, lots of photos.
A: I don't do the photos. Dean takes one of me looking miserable by the pool and that's it.
B: Ha! That's the real holiday photo, though. Mine are all fake, I'm standing there for twenty minutes.
A: What d'you watch, then, after all them nights?
B: Love Island. I'm not ashamed.
A: I watch Gogglebox. Anything with people arguing, really.
B: Yes! That's the best telly. Who's your favourite on Gogglebox?
A: The ones that hate everything.
B: Ha, of course. I think we'd get on, Tracey.
A: Yeah, you're alright.
